newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Black empowerment key to S.Africa liquor bill-govt.
newsitem.headline: Black empowerment key to S.Africa liquor bill-govt.

text.p: South Africa's trade and industry department said on Wednesday that the proposed new liquor bill aimed to correct distortions in the market brought about by past racial and restrictive policies.

Zavareh Rustomjee, trade and industry director general, said in a statement that the new legislation would give priority to black empowerment whilst government, as regulator, would try to achieve an appropriate mix of enterprise and regulation.

"The new legislation facilitates easy entry into the liquor trade, thereby empowering informal liquor traders...against whom the structure of the past and current legislation discriminate unfairly," Rustomjee said.
The statement follows comments from beer giant South African Breweries Ltd (SAB) which last week slammed key aspects of the bill as "inappropriate and practical".

Norman Adami, managing director of SAB's beer division, said the bill, which was published on July 11 and is open for public comment until August 8, would not result in the intended empowerment of previously disadvantaged communities at wholesaler level.
"The consequences of the draft bill in its present form will not match its intentions," he said.
Adami was also critical of the bill's proposal to split the producer-wholesaler link as he said wholesale distribution was an integral part of any supplier's or manufacturer's business.
The bill may also force SAB to divest its 30 percent stake in wine and spirits wholesalers Stellenbosch Farmers Winery Ltd (SFW).
SAB, the world's fifth largest brewer, controls around 97 percent of South Africa's beer market.
